transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I mean, it's just... everything has gotten so incredibly difficult lately, especially at work. I work as a hairstylist, you know, and usually, I'm pretty quick on my feet, but lately, my hands feel like they’re moving through glue. It's the strangest feeling, like I'm underwater or something. Even the simplest things, like sectioning hair for a cut or mixing color in the back room—things I've done a million times and usually do without even thinking—it just takes me forever now. I'll be standing there trying to part someone's hair, and it's like my arms are weighed down. And it's not just me noticing it, which is the worst part. The other stylists, and even some of my regular clients, have started noticing I’m just slower than I used to be. My manager pulled me aside the other day to ask if I was feeling okay because my appointment times are dragging out so much longer than they should, and I didn't even know what to tell her because I don't know why I can't just move normally anymore. It's just so frustrating because I want to go faster, my brain knows I need to go faster, but my body just won't cooperate.
Along with this physical slowness, have you noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah... yeah, I really have. Honestly, it's... it's like this constant thing now. Most days, I just wake up and before I even open my eyes, I can feel it. It's this heavy, flat sadness right here in my chest. Like an actual, physical weight just pressing down on my ribs. And it just sits there. 

I used to wake up and think about, you know, my clients for the day, or what new color trends I wanted to try out, or just... I don't know, my future. When I was getting my associate's degree, I had all these big plans about building my clientele and maybe opening my own little salon studio one day. I had everything mapped out, I even had vision boards. But lately... I just lay there in bed with that heavy feeling and I just think, what is even the point? It feels like there’s just no point in trying to build the life I was planning. It all just feels so pointless and gray now. 

I don't even care about the things I used to love doing anymore. I used to spend hours watching styling tutorials or doing my own makeup just for fun on my days off, and now I can barely even look at my palettes. I just feel so incredibly down all the time, and it's exhausting, you know? It's like I'm grieving for the life I wanted, but nothing actually happened to make me feel this way, I just... I just feel so sad from the minute my alarm goes off, and I can't seem to shake it no matter what I do or where I am.
Have you ever had periods, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, along with racing thoughts or impulsive behavior?

No, no, I've never had anything like that. I mean, I know what you're talking about, like when people get super hyper or just go on these crazy spending sprees or stay up all night cleaning their whole house from top to bottom. I had a roommate once who used to do that, she'd stay up for like three days straight painting the living room and rearranging all the furniture, and she'd talk so fast you couldn't even understand her. But no, I've never experienced anything even close to that. 

If anything, it's the exact opposite for me. I need so much sleep now, way more than I used to. I could probably sleep for fourteen hours a day if I didn't have to drag myself out of bed for work. And even when I was feeling okay, before all this heaviness started, I was just... normal, you know? I'd have good days where I had energy to go to work and maybe see a friend for coffee after, but I always needed my solid eight hours of sleep, and my thoughts were never racing or anything. I've never had a time where I felt like I was on top of the world or had all this extra energy to burn. It's just... it's just been this slow, steady decline into feeling exhausted and sad all the time. So, no, definitely no periods of feeling elated or energetic like that. Not even for a day, let alone several days.
Have you noticed any trembling or shaking in your hands, or stiffness/rigidity in your muscles, along with this slowness?

No, I haven't really noticed any shaking or trembling, like, my hands aren't vibrating or anything like that. When I'm holding my shears, my grip is steady, it's just... it's just getting them to move where I want them to go that takes so much effort. Like I said, it's that heavy feeling, like I'm moving through molasses. But they aren't shaking. 

And as for stiffness... I mean, I don't feel rigid, exactly. It's not like my joints are locked up or like I have arthritis or something where it actually hurts to bend my fingers. I had a client once who had terrible rheumatoid arthritis and her hands were so stiff she couldn't even hold a coffee cup in the morning, and it's definitely nothing like that. My muscles just feel... tired. Like they've run a marathon even when I haven't done anything. 

Sometimes I'll be standing behind the chair, and my shoulders will just feel so weighed down, almost like I'm wearing a lead vest, like the kind they put on you at the dentist when you get x-rays. But it's not a stiff feeling, it's just this profound, exhausting heaviness. I can still bend my arms and flex my hands, it just takes so much more energy to do it than it used to. So, no, no shaking, and not really stiff or rigid, just... just incredibly slow and heavy. It's so frustrating because I know how to do my job, I've been doing it every day, but my body just feels like it's made of lead now.
Have you noticed any other physical changes recently, like feeling unusually cold all the time, gaining weight without changes in eating, or your skin and hair becoming very dry or brittle?

Well, I'm definitely not cold all the time, and my skin and hair seem pretty normal. Being a cosmetologist, I'm always checking the condition of my hair and skin, you know? I use really good professional products, so I'd definitely notice if things were getting brittle or overly dry. But weight gain? No, actually, it's... it's been the opposite. 

I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything, but I've definitely noticed my clothes fitting differently. Like, my favorite pair of work pants—these black, high-waisted ones that used to fit me perfectly, almost a little snug after lunch—they're really loose now. I have to wear a belt with them or they just slide right down my hips, which is so annoying when I'm trying to focus on a client's cut. 

It's just that I haven't really had any appetite lately. It's not like I'm actively deciding not to eat, it's more like... I just forget? Or I just don't have the energy to care about food. I used to love meal prepping on Sundays. I'd make these really nice salads with grilled chicken and quinoa, and I'd pack all my lunches for the week so I'd have something healthy to eat in the breakroom. But now, the thought of standing in the kitchen and chopping vegetables just feels impossible. It's that heaviness again. 

So what happens is, I'll wake up feeling so down, and I'll just grab a large iced coffee on my way to the salon. And I'll just drink that coffee all morning. Then lunchtime comes, and maybe I'll have a few bites of a protein bar or a handful of pretzels if someone leaves them out, but nothing sounds good. Food just seems like cardboard. And then I'll get home at night, completely exhausted, and I'll realize, oh, I haven't actually eaten a real meal all day. I'll just crawl into bed because I'm too tired to cook or even order takeout. So yeah, I've definitely been skipping meals without really meaning to, just because the whole process of eating feels like too much work, and I guess that's why my clothes are getting so baggy.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks or months of feeling this same kind of sadness, low energy, and slowness—at any other point in your life, prior to this current episode?

No, honestly, never. I mean... I've never experienced anything even remotely close to this before. Like, obviously I've been sad in the past, you know? Like normal sad. When I was nineteen, my boyfriend and I broke up right before the holidays, and I was pretty devastated. I cried for probably a week straight, watched a bunch of sad movies, and didn't really want to go out with my friends. But that was just... that was a normal breakup. I still went to my classes, I still cared about getting my cosmetology license. It didn't feel like this heavy, suffocating blanket that just won't lift. 

And as for being tired, sure, cosmetology school was incredibly draining. We had so many practical exams, learning all the chemical processing and color theory, and I was trying to work part-time as a receptionist at a salon just to get my foot in the door. There were weeks where I was running on fumes, just completely wiped out. But it was a completely different kind of tired. It was a physical tiredness from actually doing things, you know? Like, if I slept in on a Sunday and just had a lazy day, I was good to go by Monday morning. I bounced right back. 

But this? This is entirely new. I've never had a time where the sadness and the slowness just dragged on for weeks and months without any real reason. It's like my battery is permanently drained to one percent and no matter how much I sleep, it won't recharge. I've always been a pretty upbeat person, always ready to chat with my clients and keep the energy up in the salon, so feeling this way is just... it's really scary because it's so completely out of left field for me. I keep waiting to just wake up and feel like my old self again, but it doesn't happen. So, no, I've never had a period of time like this before in my entire life. It's just this one time, right now, and it just feels like it's never going to end.
